overview: White answers 1.a3 a5 with 2.b4, offering the b-pawn to open the a-file and the b2 diagonal. After 2...axb4 3.axb4 Rxa1 4.Qxa1 material is level and White has the long diagonal for Bb2 against a loosened queenside. Few strong players choose it, so the play is quirky rather than theoretical.

white_ideas.idea: Open the a-file and trade rooks, then use Qa1 and Bb2 against g7
Recapture on b4 and build a centre with e3, Nf3, c4

black_ideas.idea: Take on b4, trade on a1 and develop quickly
Decline with ...e6 or ...d5 and keep a solid set-up

typical_structures.structure: Open a-file traded off, White queen on a1 and bishop on b2
Flank structure with White pawns on b4, c2, d2

character.notes: Early flank play with few forcing lines; positions are unusual but not especially sharp.

gambit.notes: 2...axb4 3.axb4 Rxa1 4.Qxa1 leaves material level, so nothing is kept; the root is not a gambit despite the name.

soundness.notes: A playable oddity; Black has easy equality but nothing is refuted.

structure.notes: Flank pawn moves with no fixed centre; the centre is settled later.

approach.notes: A rare sideline that strong players seldom pick, chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Little theory and plain plans, but not a repertoire line for White.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...axb4 main capture
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. a3 a5 2. b4 axb4 3. axb4 Rxa1 4. Qxa1
sublines_that_differ.how: Rooks trade at once and the queen takes the long diagonal

character.reason: Neither side forces matters early, and the trade of rooks leaves a quiet position.

gambit.reason: The b-pawn comes back after ...axb4 axb4 Rxa1 Qxa1 so material is level.

soundness.reason: Black equalises easily but White has no real concession.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided and both sides develop around flank pawns.

level.reason: Not hard to play, but not a line a coach recommends.

plans.reason: The b2 bishop on the long diagonal is the point of 2.b4.
